All right, let's go.

Number 10. The Bloop and the unknown leviathan.

On the morning of May 19th, 1997, hydrophones operated by the United States National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration captured something that has never been satisfactorily explained. The sound originated somewhere in the remote South Pacific, off the southern coast of Chile, in waters approximately 5,000 meters deep. It was detected simultaneously by sensors more than 5,000 kilometers apart. To register on instruments separated by that distance, the source had to be extraordinarily powerful, far louder than any recorded marine animal in history. NOAA scientists logged it, analyzed it, and gave it a name that would haunt cryptozoology for decades. They called it the Bloop.
